name: Question 11
problem:
The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. Given that $X∼N(0,{\sigma }^{2})$ is a normal random variable with $P(-2<X<2)=0.6578,$ find ${\sigma }^{2}$ rounded to $2$ decimal places.

| $z$ | $\,0.04\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.8\,$ | $\,0.7995\,$ | $\,0.8023\,$ | $\,0.8051\,$ |
| $\,0.9\,$ | $\,0.8264\,$ | $\,0.8289\,$ | $\,0.8315\,$ |
| $\,1.0\,$ | $\,0.8508\,$ | $\,0.8531\,$ | $\,0.8554\,$ |

${\sigma }^{2}≈$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
First, we find the cumulative probability using symmetry:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-2<X<2) & =0.6578 \\ 2P(0<X<2) & =0.6578 \\ P(0<X<2) & =0.3289 \\ P(X<2)-P(X<0) & =0.3289 \\ P(X<2)-0.5 & =0.3289 \\ P(X<2) & =0.8289 \\ P(X\le 2) & =0.8289\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 2) & =0.8289 \\ P\,(Z\le \frac{2-0}{\sigma }) & =0.8289 \\ Φ\,(\frac{2}{\sigma }) & =0.8289 \\ \frac{2}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.8289)\end{aligned}
$$

According to the table, we have

$$
Φ(0.95)=0.8289\,⇒\,{Φ}^{-1}(0.8289)=0.95.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sigma } & =0.95 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{2}{0.95} \\ \sigma  & ≈2.105\,26.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =(2.105\,26)^{2} \\  & ≈4.43\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
